newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 1.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Rugby union backrower Owen Finnegan and centre Adam Magro are flying to Britain to replace Wallaby centre Jason Little and backrower Michael Brial who were injured during a 47-20 win over Scotland A on Wednesday. It is unlikely Little or Brial will play again on tour, leaving Australia's increasing injury toll drawing closer to crisis point. Page 24.

After announcing allrounders Brad McNamara, of New South Wales, and Queensland's Geoff Foley are cleared of any illegal bowling actions by their respective state associations, the Australian Cricket Board will tighten the controls on the exposure of potential "chucking" offenders. Page 24.

The South East Melbourne Magic basketball team are hoping to stretch the final series of the National Basketball League to a third game as they front up against the Melbourne Tigers tonight. The Tigers won the first match in the series 100-89, yet Magic general manager Rob Nugent said his team failed to take advantage of their opportunities in that match and should win through as they are younger, stronger and fitter than their rivals. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Two Gai Waterhouse-trained horses, Nothin' Leica Dane and Magic of Sydney, showed problems while preparing for tomorrow's A$1 million Victoria Derby at Flemington, with Magic of Sydney suffering stomach pains from gas and Nothin' Leica Dane being classed as a 'windsucker' which makes it ingest air as it eats. However, Waterhouse was confident the pair will be right to race in Tuesday's Melbourne Cup. Page 42.

Point-guard Aaron Trahair will replace Shane Heal as the Sydney Kings basketball team's primary playmaker for the next three years. Trahair, a former Perth Wildcats player will join other recruits Cameron Dickinson and Matt Neilsen at the Kings. Page 41.

Women's Hockey Australia has announced the team to tour to India next month with Queenslander Jenny Morris appointed captain. Recently named women's hockey player of the year, Alyson Annan, will support Morris in her role as vice-captain. Page 39.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League is expected to endorse a plan by Essendon coach Kevin Sheedy to allow extra players on the interchange bench for next season's finals. AFL's general manager of football operations, Ian Collins, says there is a lot of merit in the idea, to ensure there are no distorted results in the most important matches of the season. Page C12.

Australia's first two Aboriginal Olympic medallists, Cathy Freeman and Nova Peris, will be training together. Although the two won medals in different sports - Freeman in athletics and Peris in hockey - Peris is setting her sights on athletics and will be trained by Freeman's coach Peter Fortune. Page C12.

While the number of New Zealand horses competing in the Melbourne Cup has waned since Northern Hemisphere horses began competing, there is one Kiwi horse, Senator, who would be a household name in Melbourne if it weren't for the discussions about favourite Oscar Schindler. Senator is rated the best stayer in New Zealand, and will arrive quietly in Melbourne tomorrow. Page C11.
HERALD SUN

Horse trainer Bart Cummings, whose Cox Plate winner Saintly will put in a bid for the trainer to win his 10th Melbourne Cup, has refused to concede the Melbourne Cup to Irish sensation Oscar Schindler. Cummings said that while Oscar Schindler may be of world-class standard, so too are a lot of the Australian horses. Page 112.

The Melbourne AFL club president Joseph Gutnick has forced anti-merger campaign leader Brian Dixon to abandon his attempts to join the Melbourne board after Gutnick threatened to pull out of the club if Dixon went ahead with it. Gutnick said he does not want to be responsible for the deterioration of the club. Page 112.

Australian golfer Robert Allenby said he was greeted with hostility and ignorance at Valderrama in Spain. Allenby, who was injured recently in a car accident, was forced to tee up in the Masters so he could pick up his A$150,000 bonus pool money, which he donated to charity. He said many players were not impressed with his appearance at the tournament. Page 101.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

At the fraud trial of former rugby union executive Ken Elphick yesterday, Elphick claimed more than 40 high-profile rugby players received secret cash endorsements to play and promote the game. He said the players were paid in the late 1980s at a time wen rugby union was an amateur sport and players could not be paid and the amounts paid ranged from A$500 to A$3,000. Page 104.

A meeting between the Australian Soccer Players' Association and Soccer Australia has ended with the Socceroos endorsing an agreement to receive a share of Soccer Australia's match tournament profits. Soccer Australia had little choice but to side with the players who were threatening strike action. Page 102.

The Australian cricket team faces a mountainous task this week if it hopes to reach the finals of the Titan Cup against India and South Africa in India. The team has not had a win on its tour of India, and captain Mark Taylor says confidence is low and the team is not playing at its peak. Page 96.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
